summary: Preserved candidate PR 2995's embedding benchmark workflows and corrected the three independently reviewed loader counterexamples: token-ID lists and batches are accepted and counted, while whitespace-only strings are rejected consistently with the serving layer.

tests.what_was_measured: At exact candidate 7f23d0cd29dafc0637e85ac6c211752948711a29 before correction, both valid token-ID forms raised ValueError and whitespace-only input was accepted with zero tokens; after correction, both token-ID forms were accepted with three tokens and whitespace-only input raised ValueError. Raw before/after output is retained outside the checkout.
All six focused embedding dataset/offline encode tests passed, including the new token-ID and whitespace regressions; two subtests passed.
The complete benchmark dataset API module passed: 51 tests and 8 subtests.
All changed Python implementation modules compiled successfully.
The consolidated working-tree diff contained no whitespace errors.

gpu_evidence: The correction concerns deterministic JSONL validation and token counting and required no model execution. Missing model weights were not treated as evidence for source changes.
remaining_limitations: The candidate's prior GPU numerical validation was not repeated because it is unrelated to the reproduced loader counterexamples and its private model artifacts are unavailable.
vLLM server interoperability was not executed.
Offline embedding mode intentionally remains limited to one string per JSONL record; token-ID arrays are supported by the online bench_serving workflow addressed by the review.
